doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Women in jazz and the business
title: Audience preconceptions of an all-women band
summary: A Midwest reviewer expected a watered-down 'In the Mood' and was won over; older women are delighted to see them.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Like kind of a novelty thing?

Yeah. We played a long midwest tour and this guy sent me an article he wrote for the paper and it said, “the last thing I wanted to do on Saturday night was go hear some all- girl band play a watered down version of ‘In the Mood.’” That was how his article started. Then he went, “oh my God I was so wrong” and then he just went on to say like how just his preconception of what women musicians were like stopped him from even wanting to go. He’s like, “my wife had to drag me by the ear,” you know. And that’s also a neat thing like a lot of the women, older women from like 60 on up, you know sometimes they’ll come to the stage and go, “I played trumpet in fifth grade, this is so great and we’re so happy to see women.” You know and like older women get really like turned on too and they’re happy to see women doing something that they didn’t necessarily see in their generation.
